title: Prove the c=1 ++ 216-space is reducible under its signed normalizer.
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Change and mathematical scope

Finite exact certificate for one joint eigenspace of the historical doubled centre block at `c=1`. The trivial sign character splits into four 216-dimensional joint spaces under the involutions `g` and `t` from PR #6944. The centralizer of `{g,t}` in the signed-permutation stabilizer has order 16 and acts by `±I` on every one of those spaces. That exhaustive count is not an irreducibility proof.

The normalizer has order 96. Its image on the trivial-character `(+1,+1)` space is the dihedral group of order 12, with rational `A_1`-invariant isotypic dimensions **8**, **80**, and **128**. The same normalizer cuts each of the other three 216-spaces as 72+144. The `(+1,+1)` summand is reducible under `A_1`.

No new kappa. The selected conditional kappa stays `781451/250000000`. This package does not compute a characteristic polynomial.

## Task and overlap

- Task: `formal-interface-lemma`, scope changed.
- Upstream base: `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` (priority revision 8). This fork PR is based on that pin.
- Handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19144258
- Predecessor: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6944
- Package: `research/centre-216-normalizer-split/`

The catalogue card asks for a formal caller binding. The handoff, left open by #6944, asks whether one 216-dimensional summand is irreducible under `A_1`. This package answers that question for the trivial-character `(+1,+1)` summand.

Overlap on 2026-11-10: 895 open PRs and 6934 discussion records, pagination complete; local notes 8917 of 8917, complete. The phrase `216-dimensional` matches #6944 and no other open PR. The fork branch `cursor/a1-joint-216-charpoly-0702` at `306f791048636c7dc91c83ecb8ae6e730908042c` computes the characteristic polynomial of the same 216-space and records the factors `x` and `x-2`. That shows reducibility without a subspace or a centralizer census. This package does not read those coefficients and does not identify the 8-dimensional symmetry summand with a factor of that polynomial.

## Validation

CPython 3.12.3, standard library only.

```sh
python3 -B -W error research/centre-216-normalizer-split/verify.py
python3 -B -O research/centre-216-normalizer-split/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre-216-normalizer-split --check-only
```

Marker: `PASS_CENTRE_216_NORMALIZER_SPLIT`. Both modes passed. Metadata check returned `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. Selected baseline returned `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.

The line-preserving signed-permutation group has order 344064 and index 30 in the hyperoctahedral group. The `c=1` stabilizer has order 3072. Rejection controls cover a coordinate transposition, the incomplete swap of coordinates 4 and 7, a swapped port label, and a sign symmetry that does not commute with `g`.

Not run: Lean, Docker, the degree-881 replay, any characteristic polynomial, and the selected cold replay.

## Credit

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance.

JoyboyBrian recorded the sign-character dimensions and the open 432-coordinate question. PR #6944 split the trivial `c=1` character into 216-dimensional blocks and left irreducibility open. Ali Romman's PR4958 and PR4720 retain the query and the Bell action. Krzysztof Wojt's `research/exact-one-slot-gram/` supplies the 13 generators and the degree-881 annihilator. Nick Petalas's PR5120 is the degree-410 lower bound. The doubled representation comes from PR1719. New work is Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

See `research/centre-216-normalizer-split/TASK.json`.

- Is the 8-dimensional isotypic summand irreducible under `A_1`? The character inner product gives the dimension and does not list a basis. A missing further involution would not decide it.
- Does any signed permutation in the `c=1` stabilizer, outside the normalizer of `{g,t}`, preserve that summand and act non-scalarly?
